source_metadata.answer: A beef patty is 'done' when it reaches an internal temperature of 160°F (71°C), which typically takes about 4 minutes on each side when cooking on medium-high heat. The patty should be browned on the outside with no pink visible on the inside. You can verify doneness by using a meat thermometer or checking that the juices run clear when pressing down on the center of the patty.
